title: The rays gather into the sun
hookLine: at sunset the sun's rays gather back into the sun, and an Upanishad says the senses do the same at night
carry: pratyahara: the senses drawn back in

lines: FIREWOOD IN HAND. A YEAR OF WAITING.
THE RAYS GATHER INTO THE SUN.
cards: Six seekers walk to a sage's hermitage with firewood in their hands, the old sign of students asking to be taught. The sage, Pippalada, tells them: live here a year first, then ask.
A year later, one of them, Gargya, asks about the body at night. When a person sleeps, what is it in them that sleeps? And what stays awake?
Pippalada answers with the evening sky. At sunset, he says, the rays of the sun all gather back into that one disc of light. At sunrise they spread out again.
That's what happens to the senses every night.

teach.h: THE SENSES BECOME ONE IN THE MIND.
teach.b: That's the Prashna Upanishad, the Upanishad of Questions, and the fourth question is Gargya's.
Pippalada's answer, in paraphrase: as the rays of the setting sun become one in its disc of light, so in sleep all the senses become one in the mind, the highest of them.
Then the person doesn't hear, see, smell, taste or touch, speak, take hold or move. And people say, he sleeps.

teach.h: THE BREATHS KEEP WATCH, LIKE FIRES.
teach.b: Yet the breaths keep watch in the city of the body, like fires kept burning in a house.

teach.h: THE SENSES ARE INSTRUMENTS, NOT THE SELF.
teach.b: Under the picture sits a teaching Hindu schools share: the senses are the mind's instruments, sent out by day, not the self that sends them. Sleep gathers them in without asking.
Patanjali has a name for gathering them in on purpose, while awake.
In the second chapter of the Yoga Sutras he calls it pratyahara: the senses withdrawing from their objects and following the mind inward. The Gita gives the picture: a tortoise drawing in its limbs.
Satyananda describes yoga nidra as a way into pratyahara, and the main tool is a quick tour of the body called the rotation of awareness.
The guide names a part, the right-hand thumb, the palm, the wrist, and the listener places attention there, without moving. It looks like doing very little.

teach.h: THE RAYS GATHER INTO THE SUN.
teach.b: But it's the senses being gathered back into the mind, the way Pippalada saw the rays gathered into the sun, only this time on purpose.

how: In guided yoga nidra, the teacher names parts of the body in a set order and listeners place attention on each without moving; teachers describe this rotation of awareness as a doorway to pratyahara, the withdrawal of the senses.

o: a sleep so light that every sound wakes you
the sleep of yoga, with the senses drawn inward
stretching each body part before you nap

games.q: the gathering in — tap the pairs.
p: the sage of the Prashna Upanishad
the rays gather into the sun
the senses become one in the mind
the senses drawn in, on purpose

s: in the Prashna Upanishad, everything in a person shuts down in sleep
the senses gather into the mind, but the breaths keep watch in the body, like fires kept burning.
the rotation of awareness asks the listener to move each part named
the listener places attention on each part without moving it.
Patanjali's word for drawing the senses inward is pratyahara
in the second chapter of the Yoga Sutras, the senses withdraw from their objects and follow the mind inward.

games.q: the guide says: right-hand thumb. what do you do?
o: wiggle it, to be sure it's there.
games.why: in the rotation of awareness you simply rest attention on the part named, then move on. The senses quiet, and attention watches them gather in.

practice: Lie down or sit back with eyes closed, and without moving, let attention go where it's named: right-hand thumb, second finger, third, fourth, fifth, palm, back of the hand, wrist, elbow, shoulder, right side of the chest, right hip, knee, ankle, right big toe.
Now the whole right side, all at once. Then let attention rest on the breath, keeping watch, like a fire kept burning in a house.

wordCard.voice: Yoga nidra. The sleep of yoga, where pratyahara gathers the senses into the mind, like rays into the setting sun, this time on purpose.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: pratyahara, the drawing in of the senses. In the Yoga Sutras, the limb of yoga before concentration.

carryVoice: Your line: pratyahara, the senses drawn back in, like rays into the setting sun. Tomorrow, the one who stays awake. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Swami Satyananda Saraswati, Yoga Nidra (Bihar School of Yoga)
